text: The number of ways in which 21 identical apples can be distributed among three children such that each child gets at least 2 apples, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we can use a classic combinatorics method known as "stars and bars" (or "balls and bins"), which is a way to solve problems involving distributing identical items into distinct groups with certain restrictions.

First, since each child must get at least 2 apples, let's give 2 apples to each child right away. That accounts for 6 apples (2 apples for each of the 3 children). Now, we have 21 - 6 = 15 apples left to distribute freely among the three children.

The "stars and bars" technique involves representing the apples as stars (*) and the divisions between children as bars (|). For example, if we had 5 apples to distribute among three children, one possible distribution could be represented as **|*|**. This means the first child gets 2 apples, the second child gets 1 apple, and the third child gets 2 apples.

In our case, we need to distribute 15 apples (stars) among the three children with 2 bars to create the partitions. We arrange 15 stars and 2 bars in a row, where the arrangement of stars and bars corresponds to a distribution of the apples.

The total number of objects we're arranging is 15 apples + 2 bars = 17 objects. We need to choose 2 positions out of these 17 to place the bars. The remaining positions will be occupied by the stars (apples).

The number of ways to choose 2 positions out of 17 for the bars is given by the binomial coefficient:

$\text{Number of ways}=\left (17 2\right )=\frac{17!}{2!(17-2)!}=\frac{17\times 16}{2\times 1}=136$

Thus, there are 136 ways to distribute the 21 identical apples among three children such that each child gets at least 2 apples. The correct answer is Option B: 136.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A coin is biased so that a head is twice as likely to occur as a tail. If the coin is tossed 3 times, then the probability of getting two tails and one head is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we need to first determine the probability of getting a head (H) and the probability of getting a tail (T).

Since a head is twice as likely to occur as a tail, we can denote the probability of getting a tail as $P(T)=p$ and the probability of getting a head as $P(H)=2p$.

These probabilities must sum to 1 because those are the only two possible outcomes for each coin toss :

$P(H)+P(T)=1$

$2p+p=1$

$3p=1$

$p=\frac{1}{3}$

Therefore, the probability of getting a tail (T) is $P(T)=\frac{1}{3}$ and the probability of getting a head (H) is $P(H)=2\times \frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$.

Now to find the probability of getting two tails and one head, we need to consider the different sequences in which this can occur. There are three unique sequences: TTH, THT, and HTT.

The probability of each sequence is found by multiplying the probabilities of each individual event since each coin toss is independent:

$P(TTH)=P(T)\times P(T)\times P(H)=\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{2}\times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{9}\times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{2}{27}$

$P(THT)=P(T)\times P(H)\times P(T)=\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{2}{3}\times \frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{27}$

$P(HTT)=P(H)\times P(T)\times P(T)=\frac{2}{3}\times \left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{2}=\frac{2}{27}$

The overall probability of getting two tails and one head in any order is the sum of these individual probabilities :

$P(2T1H)=P(TTH)+P(THT)+P(HTT)=\frac{2}{27}+\frac{2}{27}+\frac{2}{27}=\frac{6}{27}$

Simplifying this expression gives us:
$P(2T1H)=\frac{6}{27}=\frac{2}{9}$

Therefore, the correct answer is :

Option B :
$\frac{2}{9}$

text:
Let $A$ be a $3\times 3$ real matrix such that

$A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=2⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟,A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=4⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟,A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=2⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟\text{.}$

Then, the system $(A-3I)⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$ has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Adding and subtracting the first two given relations:

$A\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{l} -4 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} -2 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{array}\right ],A\left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]-\left [\begin{array}{l} -4 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 6 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{array}\right ]$

So the first and third columns of $A$ are $(3,0,-1)^{T}$ and $(-1,0,3)^{T}$. The third relation gives the second column $(0,2,0)^{T}$:

$A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \end{array}\right ],A-3I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$|A-3I|=(-1)\left |\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{array}\right |=(-1)(0-1)=1\neq 0$

Since $A-3I$ is non-singular, the system has exactly one solution, given by $-z=1$, $-y=2$, $-x=3$, that is, $(x,y,z)=(-3,-2,-1)$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let $P$ be a parabola with vertex $(2,3)$ and directrix $2x+y=6$. Let an ellipse $E:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1,a>b$, of eccentricity $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ pass through the focus of the parabola $P$. Then, the square of the length of the latus rectum of $E$, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The axis of the parabola passes through the vertex $V(2,3)$ perpendicular to the directrix $2x+y=6$ (slope $-2$), so its slope is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and its equation is $x-2y+4=0$.

The axis meets the directrix at $Z$: solving $x-2y+4=0$ and $2x+y-6=0$ gives $Z=(1.6,2.8)$.

The vertex is the midpoint of $Z$ and the focus $S(α,β)$:

$\dfrac{α+1.6}{2}=2,\dfrac{β+2.8}{2}=3\Rightarrow S=(2.4,3.2)=\left (\dfrac{12}{5},\dfrac{16}{5}\right )$

For $E$, $e^{2}=1-\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow a^{2}=2b^{2}$. Since $E$ passes through $S$:

$\dfrac{144}{25\cdot 2b^{2}}+\dfrac{256}{25\quad b^{2}}=1\Rightarrow \dfrac{72+256}{25\quad b^{2}}=1\Rightarrow b^{2}=\dfrac{328}{25}$

Square of the latus rectum:

$\left (\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{4b^{4}}{a^{2}}=\dfrac{4b^{4}}{2b^{2}}=2b^{2}=\dfrac{656}{25}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take $e^{\sin x}=t(t>0)$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}-\dfrac{2}{\mathrm{t}}=2 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{t}^{2}-2}{\mathrm{t}}=2 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}^{2}-2\mathrm{t}-2=0 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}^{2}-2\mathrm{t}+1=3 \\ \Rightarrow (\mathrm{t}-1)^{2}=3 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=1\pm \sqrt{3} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=1\pm 1.73 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=2.73\text{or}-0.73\text{(rejected as}\mathrm{t}>0) \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}=2.73 \\ \Rightarrow \log _{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}=\log _{\mathrm{e}}2.73 \\ \Rightarrow \sin \mathrm{x}=\log _{\mathrm{e}}2.73>1 \end{array}$

So no solution.

text: Let $f,g:(0,\infty )\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be two functions defined by $f(x)=\int\limits _{-x}^{x}\left (|t|-t^{2}\right )e^{-t^{2}}dt$ and $g(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x^{2}}t^{1/2}e^{-t}dt$. Then, the value of $9\left (f\left (\sqrt{\log _{e}9}\right )+g\left (\sqrt{\log _{e}9}\right )\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $(|t|-t^{2})e^{-t^{2}}$ is an even function of $t$, for $x>0$

$f(x)=2\int\limits _{0}^{x}\left (t-t^{2}\right )e^{-t^{2}}dt$

In $g(x)$, put $t=u^{2}$, $dt=2udu$ (so $t^{1/2}=u$); the limits become $0$ to $x$:

$g(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}ue^{-u^{2}}\cdot 2udu=2\int\limits _{0}^{x}u^{2}e^{-u^{2}}du$

Adding, the $t^{2}e^{-t^{2}}$ terms cancel:

$f(x)+g(x)=2\int\limits _{0}^{x}te^{-t^{2}}dt=\left [-e^{-t^{2}}\right ]_{0}^{x}=1-e^{-x^{2}}$

At $x=\sqrt{\log _{e}9}$, $e^{-x^{2}}=e^{-\log _{e}9}=\dfrac{1}{9}$, so $f(x)+g(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{9}=\dfrac{8}{9}$ and

$9\left (f\left (\sqrt{\log _{e}9}\right )+g\left (\sqrt{\log _{e}9}\right )\right )=8$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to (0,\infty )$ be a strictly increasing function such that $\lim _{x\to \infty }\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}=1$. Then, the value of $\lim _{x\to \infty }\left [\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}-1\right ]$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x>0$, $x<5x<7x$; since $f$ is strictly increasing and $f(x)>0$,

$1<\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}<\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}\Rightarrow 0<\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}-1<\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}-1.$

As $x\to \infty$, $\dfrac{f(7x)}{f(x)}-1\to 1-1=0$, so by the sandwich theorem $\dfrac{f(5x)}{f(x)}-1\to 0$.

If $[\cdot ]$ is read as the greatest integer function, the same inequality gives $0<\dfrac{f(5x)}{f(x)}-1<1$ for all large $x$, so the bracket equals $0$ there and the limit is again $0$.

$\lim _{x\to \infty }\left [\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}-1\right ]=0$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

$⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \end{array}\right |=7\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$

so the right side is $2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})+24\hat{j}-6\hat{k}=14\hat{i}+10\hat{j}-20\hat{k}$.

With $⃗{c}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$,

$(5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\times ⃗{c}=(z-4y)\hat{i}+(4x-5z)\hat{j}+(5y-x)\hat{k}$

Comparing components: $z-4y=14$, $4x-5z=10$, $5y-x=-20$. The first and third give $z=4y+14$ and $x=5y+20$, and the second then holds identically, so one more condition is needed.

$⃗{a}-⃗{b}+\hat{i}=(3-2+1)\hat{i}+(2+1)\hat{j}+(1-3)\hat{k}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, so $2x+3y-2z=-3$.

Substituting: $2(5y+20)+3y-2(4y+14)=5y+12=-3\Rightarrow y=-3$, hence $x=5$ and $z=2$.

$|⃗{c}|^{2}=25+9+4=38$

Hence, the answer is 38.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation 

$\sec ^{2}xdx+\left (e^{2y}\tan ^{2}x+\tan x\right )dy=0,0<x<\frac{π}{2},y(π/4)=0$. 

If $y(π/6)=α$, then $e^{8α}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \sec ^{2}x\dfrac{dx}{dy}+e^{2y}\tan ^{2}x+\tan x=0 \\ \left (\text{Put}\tan x=t\Rightarrow \sec ^{2}x\dfrac{dx}{dy}=\dfrac{dt}{dy}\right ) \\ \dfrac{dt}{dy}+e^{2y}\times t^{2}+t=0 \\ \dfrac{dt}{dy}+t=-t^{2}\cdot e^{2y} \\ \dfrac{1}{t^{2}}\dfrac{dt}{dy}+\dfrac{1}{t}=-e^{2y} \\ \left (\text{Put}\dfrac{1}{t}=u\dfrac{-1}{t^{2}}\dfrac{dt}{dy}=\dfrac{du}{dy}\right ) \\ \dfrac{-du}{dy}+u=-e^{2y} \\ \dfrac{du}{dy}-u=e^{2y} \\ \text{I.F.}=e^{-\int dy}=e^{-y} \\ ue^{-y}=\int e^{-y}\times e^{2y}dy \\ \dfrac{1}{\tan x}\times e^{-y}=e^{y}+c \\ x=\dfrac{π}{4},y=0,c=0 \\ \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}=\dfrac{π}{6},\mathrm{y}=α \\ \sqrt{3}\mathrm{e}^{-α}=\mathrm{e}^{α}+0 \\ \mathrm{e}^{2α}=\sqrt{3} \\ \mathrm{e}^{8α}=9 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: $\left |\frac{120}{π^{3}}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{x^{2}\sin x\cos x}{\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x}dx\right |$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $g(x)=\dfrac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x}$, $g(π-x)=-g(x)$ and $g\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )=g(x)$.

Splitting $\int\limits _{0}^{π}$ at $\dfrac{π}{2}$ and putting $x\to π-x$ in the second part:

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}x^{2}g(x)dx=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\left [x^{2}-(π-x)^{2}\right ]g(x)dx=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\left (2πx-π^{2}\right )g(x)dx$

With $J=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}g(x)dx$, the property $x\to \dfrac{π}{2}-x$ gives $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}x\qquad g(x)dx=\dfrac{π}{4}J$. So

$I=2π\cdot \dfrac{π}{4}J-π^{2}J=-\dfrac{π^{2}}{2}J$

Dividing numerator and denominator of $g$ by $\cos ^{4}x$: $J=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{\tan x\sec ^{2}x}{1+\tan ^{4}x}dx$. Substituting $u=\tan ^{2}x$, $du=2\tan x\sec ^{2}xdx$:

$J=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\dfrac{du}{1+u^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{π}{2}=\dfrac{π}{4}$

$I=-\dfrac{π^{2}}{2}\cdot \dfrac{π}{4}=-\dfrac{π^{3}}{8}\Rightarrow \left |\dfrac{120}{π^{3}}I\right |=\dfrac{120}{8}=15$

Hence, the answer is 15.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Let $A(-2,-1),B(1,0),C(α,β)$ and $D(γ,δ)$ be the vertices of a parallelogram $ABCD$. If the point $C$ lies on $2x-y=5$ and the point $D$ lies on $3x-2y=6$, then the value of $|α+β+γ+δ|$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}\equiv \left (\dfrac{α-2}{2},\dfrac{β-1}{2}\right )\equiv \left (\dfrac{γ+1}{2},\dfrac{δ}{2}\right ) \\ \dfrac{α-2}{2}=\dfrac{γ+1}{2}\text{and}\dfrac{β-1}{2}=\dfrac{δ}{2} \\ \Rightarrow α-γ=3\ldots .(1),β-δ=1\ldots \ldots (2) \end{array}$

Also, $(γ,δ)$ lies on $3x-2y=6$

$3γ-2δ=6$ ..... (3)

and $(α,β)$ lies on $2x-y=5$

$\Rightarrow 2α-β=5\text{.}$

Solving (1), (2), (3), (4)

$\begin{array}{l} α=-3,β=-11,γ=-6,δ=-12 \\ |α+β+γ+δ|=32 \end{array}$

text: Let $a,b,c$ be the lengths of three sides of a triangle satisfying the condition $\left (a^{2}+b^{2}\right )x^{2}-2b(a+c)x+\left (b^{2}+c^{2}\right )=0$. If the set of all possible values of $x$ is the interval $(α,β)$, then $12\left (α^{2}+β^{2}\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (a^{2}+b^{2}\right )x^{2}-2b(a+c)x+b^{2}+c^{2}=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow a^{2}x^{2}-2abx+b^{2}+b^{2}x^{2}-2bcx+c^{2}=0 \\ \Rightarrow (ax-b)^{2}+(bx-c)^{2}=0 \\ \Rightarrow ax-b=0,bx-c=0 \\ \Rightarrow a+b>cb+c>ac+a>b \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lll} a+ax>bx & ax+bx>a & ax^{2}+a>ax \\ a+ax>ax^{2} & ax+ax^{2}>a & x^{2}-x+1>0 \\ x^{2}-x-1<0 & x^{2}+x-1>0 & \text{always true} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}<x<\dfrac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2} \\ x<\dfrac{-1-\sqrt{5}}{2},\text{or}x>\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{5}}{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}<x<\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow α=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2},β=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2} \\ 12\left (α^{2}+β^{2}\right )=12\left (\dfrac{(\sqrt{5}-1)^{2}+(\sqrt{5}+1)^{2}}{4}\right )=36 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: If $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{ax^{2}e^{x}-b\log _{e}(1+x)+cxe^{-x}}{x^{2}\sin x}=1$, then $16\left (a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}\right )$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{ax^{2}\left (1+x+\frac{x2}{2!}+\frac{x3}{3!}+....\right )-b\left (x-\frac{x2}{2}+\frac{x3}{3}-.....\right )+cx\left (1-x+\frac{x2}{2!}-\frac{x3}{3!}+.....\right )}{x^{3}.\frac{\sin x}{x}}$

$=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{(c-b)x+\left (\frac{b}{2}-c+a\right )x^{2}+\left (a-\frac{b}{3}+\frac{c}{2}\right )x^{3}+\ldots \ldots }{x^{3}}=1$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{c}-\mathrm{b}=0,\dfrac{\mathrm{b}}{2}-\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{a}=0 \\ \mathrm{a}-\dfrac{\mathrm{b}}{3}+\dfrac{\mathrm{c}}{2}=1\mathrm{a}=\dfrac{3}{4}\mathrm{b}=\mathrm{c}=\dfrac{3}{2} \\ \mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{c}^{2}=\dfrac{9}{16}+\dfrac{9}{4}+\dfrac{9}{4} \\ 16\left (\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{c}^{2}\right )=81 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Let A be a $3\times 3$ matrix and $\det (A)=2$. If $n=\det (\mathrm{adj}(\mathrm{adj}(\ldots ..(\mathrm{adj}A))_{2024-\text{times}}))$, then the remainder when $n$ is divided by 9 is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a matrix $X$ of order 3, $|\mathrm{adj}X|=|X|^{2}$. Applying this 2024 times,

$n=|A|^{2^{2024}}=2^{2^{2024}}.$

Since $2^{3}=8\equiv -1(\mathrm{mod}9)$, $2^{6}\equiv 1(\mathrm{mod}9)$, so only the exponent modulo 6 matters.

$2^{2024}$ is even, and $2^{2024}=(3-1)^{2024}\equiv 1(\mathrm{mod}3)$; hence $2^{2024}\equiv 4(\mathrm{mod}6)$, that is, $2^{2024}=6k+4$ for an integer $k$.

$n=2^{6k+4}=\left (2^{6}\right )^{k}\cdot 16\equiv 16\equiv 7(\mathrm{mod}9).$

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A line passes through $A(4,-6,-2)$ and $B(16,-2,4)$. The point $P(a,b,c)$, where $a,b,c$ are non-negative integers, on the line $AB$ lies at a distance of 21 units, from the point $A$. The distance between the points $P(a,b,c)$ and $Q(4,-12,3)$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$AB\leftarrow =(16-4)\hat{i}+(-2+6)\hat{j}+(4+2)\hat{k}=12\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$, so $AB=\sqrt{144+16+36}=14$ and the unit vector along $AB$ is $\dfrac{6\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}}{7}$.

A point on line $AB$ at a distance of 21 units from $A$ is

$(4,-6,-2)\pm 21\cdot \dfrac{(6,2,3)}{7}=(4,-6,-2)\pm (18,6,9)$

This gives $(22,0,7)$ or $(-14,-12,-11)$. Only $(22,0,7)$ has non-negative integer coordinates, so $P=(22,0,7)$.

$QP\leftarrow =(22-4,0+12,7-3)=(18,12,4)$, so

$PQ=\sqrt{18^{2}+12^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{324+144+16}=\sqrt{484}=22$

Hence, the answer is 22.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift
